user.title: UE Boom
user.description:
Select your UE Boom speaker from the nearby Bluetooth devices detected by Home Assistant.

If your speaker is not listed: it must be turned **off** (in standby) to advertise over BLE. A speaker that is powered on uses classic Bluetooth and cannot be discovered this way. Turn it off, wait a few seconds, then go back and try again.

manual.title: UE Boom
manual.description:
Enter the Bluetooth MAC address of your UE Boom speaker, for example `AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF`.

The speaker must be turned **off** (in standby) to be reachable.

**How to find the address:**
- **Easiest (any platform):** while the speaker is in standby, scan with a BLE app such as nRF Connect or LightBlue — the speaker advertises as a UE/BOOM device and its MAC is displayed.
- **macOS:** hold ⌥ Option and click the Bluetooth icon in the menu bar.
- **Windows:** Device Manager → Bluetooth → your speaker → Properties → Details → "Bluetooth radio address".
- **Android:** Settings → Connected devices → tap the gear next to "BOOM" (the address may be shown), otherwise use a BLE scanner app.
- **iOS:** iOS does not expose Bluetooth MAC addresses — use a BLE scanner app.

trusted_mac.title: Trusted device
trusted_mac.description:
Enter the MAC address of a device authorized to turn the speaker on/off remotely (speaker: {address}). This is the Bluetooth MAC of the phone or computer you paired in the UE Boom app's "Remote power on" setting.

- **iOS:** Settings → General → About → Bluetooth.
- **Android:** Settings → About phone → Status → Bluetooth address (varies by manufacturer).
- **macOS:** hold ⌥ Option and click the Bluetooth icon in the menu bar (your Mac's address).
- **Windows:** Device Manager → Bluetooth → your adapter → Properties → Details → "Bluetooth radio address".

error.invalid_mac: Invalid MAC address — only 0-9 and A-F are allowed (the letter O is not a valid hex character, use the digit 0)
